statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language and Latin script; no specific transliteration required

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SAS entities provided the address is functional for correspondence and complies with anti-abuse provisions; common for professional services including staffing agencies

Legal due diligence and compliance advisory

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-27 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Decree No. 2023-1107 (ordinary and simplified forms); Articles L.210-2 and L.210-6 (constitution formalities); Decree No. 2021-300 governing the Guichet Unique filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the department of the registered office; final entry in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier de constitution (single-form incorporation file) comprising the signed Statuts (Articles of Association), capital deposit certificate, legal-notice attestation, presidential declarations and the necessary registers annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SAS (may be incorporated with €1). The full subscribed nominal capital must be deposited before registration and placed in a blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds) is required in the filing. Any in-kind contribution exceeding a stake of 50% or where a general meeting so decides requires a Commissaire aux Apports report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDER OF [COMPANY NAME] SAS, DATED [DATE]. The sole founding shareholder resolves that all issued shares have been fully subscribed and paid in; that the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles; and that the first President of the Company is appointed in the person of [FULL NAME], nationality [−], domiciled at [−], to serve for the entire duration of the Company with the widest powers to bind the Company to third parties. The shareholder further approves the opening of all French bank and payroll accounts and authorizes the President to complete the Guichet Unique filing, the Kbis formalities and all employment-law declarations required for the global EOR staffing and cross-border contractor payroll activity upon statutory formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and dating of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders together with the first President; a Notaire is mandatory only for notarial acts or real-estate/in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French (an official French translation is required if prepared in another language). The document must state the corporate name, legal form (SAS), registered-office address, corporate object expressly covering ISIC 7810 employer-of-record and cross-border contractor payroll services, amount of share capital, number and par value of shares, subscription terms, duration (usually 99 years), and the identity of the first President. Every founder must sign the final version; for in-kind contributions attach a valuation report and a notarial deed where applicable.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (Articles of Association)
Passport or residence permit of each founder
Declaration of non-conviction (bilan de déclaration) of the first President
Commissaire aux Apports report and deed of contribution where in-kind transfers are made
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the object clause as unlawful or insufficiently precise for staffing/EOR activity, amend the Statuts by a formal shareholders' decision, re-sign, and re-submit with the corrected wording.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of subscribed capital into a blocked account and issuance of the deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (blocked funds account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribing shareholders transfer the full subscription amount to a blocked account opened in the name of the company being formed. The depositary institution issues a certificate of deposit (certificat de dépôt des fonds) evidencing that the capital is held and unfrozen only upon presentation of the Kbis extract. This certificate is uploaded to the Guichet Unique and is indispensable for registration; even where capital is set at €1, the deposit procedure applies to the declared amount.
required_dossiers: Draft or pending Statuts
Bank account-opening application and KYC documentation of all subscribers
Shareholder subscription and payment schedule (tableau de souscription)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of bank delay or refusal, open the blocked account with another credit institution; the deposit certificate is freely reissued by the selected bank and remains valid until the Guichet Unique filing is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of a statutory announcement in a legal announcements gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal-announcements newspaper (JAL) authorized by the Préfecture in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the two weeks preceding the filing, publish in the JAL a notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered-office address, corporate purpose, duration and the date of signature of the Statuts. The gazette issues an attestation de parution identifying the exact date and issue, which must be uploaded to the Guichet Unique. Publication must be in the department of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Mandate addressed to the JAL editor
Proposed announcement text in compliance with legal-display rules
Final signed Statuts
Attestation de parution issued by the gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is refused for non-compliant content, correct the notice and republish immediately; the Guichet Unique filing will be rejected without a valid attestation de parution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of the complete incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), transmitted to the designated Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Connect to the official single-window portal, select company creation and the SAS model, fill in the declaration forms, upload all mandatory documents, and pay the electronic registration fee. The INPI performs a completeness check and routes the dossier to the registry office. Direct filing with the Greffe is not permitted since the Guichet Unique became mandatory.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts
Capital deposit certificate (certificat de dépôt des fonds)
JAL publication attestation
Occupancy title for the registered office (lease, rental contract or domiciliation agreement)
Acceptance of office and identity document of the first President
Beneficial-ownership declaration (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
Power of attorney if filing is made through a legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI notifies an 'incomplete dossier', a 15-day curing window is granted; correct and resubmit all deficient items within that period. If the deadline lapses, create and submit a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and issuance of the Kbis extract and company identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) at the seat of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal conformity review, the Greffe registers the SAS in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, assigns the SIREN and SIRET numbers via INSEE with the corresponding APE/NAF code, and issues the critical Kbis extract. The Kbis constitutes formal corporate existence, authority of the President, and the company's full identity. The certificate is used to open the payroll account, enroll with URSSAF and conclude client EOR contracts.
required_dossiers: Approved dossier routed by the Guichet Unique
Receipt of payment of the registration fee
Any additional documents requested by the Greffe during conformity screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Greffe issues a query or refusal, cure the identified defect by supplementary filings in the prescribed period; a registry refusal may be appealed before the President of the Commercial Court in summary proceedings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF for employer registration and DPAE; Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) for the staffing placement authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the company as an employer with URSSAF, declare the first employee through the DPAE (déclaration préalable à l'embauche), register with the specialised occupational-health service and prepare payroll rails (Local Payroll Direct Debit and Wise). Since the enterprise operates a global EOR and staffing placement platform, it must also apply for the DREETS authorization before soliciting client-placed employees. The DREETS file includes the Kbis, financial guarantees for salary liabilities and a compliance program for cross-border contractor work. Tacit approval may apply after the statutory review period.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
DREETS application form for placement agency authorization
Financial guarantee commitment (caution bancaire or approved guarantee fund)
Business plan and operational compliance manual for EOR and contractor payroll
Criminal record of the legal representative (casier judiciaire)
Registration certificate with the occupational-health service (SPSTI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DREETS refuses, file a formal recours gracieux before the same authority and a recours hiérarchique before the Minister of Labour, followed by an appeal before the Administrative Tribunal; commercial staffing operations must remain dormant until authorization is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) — Labour and Employment Control Unit (Ministry of Labour)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exercice d'activité d'agence de placement et d'entreprise de travail temporaire (Code du travail, Articles L.5321-1 et seq. and L.1251-7-1)

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) — Préfecture / Ministry for Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Registration category — no full environmental impact assessment is required for a typical administrative office and payroll platform; the activity is treated as 'non-ICPE' unless energy or backup infrastructure exceeds thresholds of the ICPE nomenclature, in which case a declaration dossier under the Code de l'environnement is submitted.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Near-zero industrial discharge regime; compliance with Code de l'environnement Articles L.541-1-1 and L.541-1-2 on mandatory waste sorting (paper, electronics, IT equipment) and with the AGEC circular-economy obligations; application of the 'décret tertiaire' energy reduction scheme where office floor area exceeds 1,000 m²; ventilation and indoor-air standards under Code du travail Articles R.4212-1 et seq. limit VOC and carbon-dioxide concentrations in all occupied office zones.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification and evacuation compliance per Code du travail Articles R.4216-1 to R.4216-34, including tested alarm systems, emergency exits, portable extinguishers and evacuation drills; for establishments open to the public, the conformity declaration issued by the Prefectoral Commission de Sécurité is required. Structural-load and occupancy clearance is evidenced by the office lease confirming the building's intended use and load capacity, together with a verification of electrical installations by an approved technical inspector. Prior to any hiring, the company must register with the occupational-health service (SPSTI), obtain the medical-fitness visiting plan and post the internal regulations in a place accessible to all posted and local employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; centralized digital portal: impots.gouv.fr and the dedicated EU VAT/OSS portal 'Le Suivi du formulaire' via the 'Pro' professional space, with the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) hosted on Chorus Pro for e-invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SAS obtains a SIREN (unique business identifier) and SIRET (establishment identifier) upon registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). Following successful incorporation, the SAS must file the 'Déclaration d'existence' with DGFiP and apply for a French VAT number ('Numéro de TVA intracommunautaire') on Form 3557-SD via the impots.gouv.fr professional portal. For foreign non-established businesses supplying taxable services in France without a permanent establishment, a direct French VAT registration is obtained by filing Form 3557-SD (with annexes) with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), or, for distance sales and certain cross-border B2C services, registration under the European Union One-Stop-Shop (IOSS/OSS) may be used instead of a full French VAT ID; in all cases, third-party written authorization and a domestic fiscal representative may be required for non-EU entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at the standard rate of 25% on its worldwide profits insofar as they are attributable to French operations, regardless of distribution; by election a newly created SAS may be taxed at the income-tax level (IR) for the first five fiscal years or indefinitely in certain holding-company situations, but the default statutory regime is entity-level corporate taxation, denial of the check-the-box pass-through treatment except for the civil partnership (SCI) option; territorial scope: France applies a narrowly construed territoriality principle for corporate tax, taxing only profits attributable to French establishments and French-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the CGI, the SAS may: (i) irrevocably elect the 'option pour l'impôt sur les sociétés' if structured as an SELAS into an entity taxed as an IR partnership (Article 239 bis, 239 ter CGI) or, for newly created SMEs, elect IR taxation on the first five fiscal years (Article 239 quater CGI); (ii) elect for French tax consolidation under Article 223 A CGI ('régime d'intégration fiscale') provided the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary; (iii) elect for the payment of VAT by the 'régime réel normal' versus the simplified 'régime réel simplifié'; (iv) elect for the franchise en base de TVA (small-business VAT exemption) if under statutory thresholds, subject to a five-year renewal election; and (v) file a hybrid-mismatch declaration (Déclaration 2258-SD) to align with the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) rules on hybrid mismatches; there is no analogous US-style Check-the-Box regime, but a hybrid entity's tax transparency is governed by Articles 8, 1655 ter and the 1998 OECD partnership report, and by administrative doctrine BOI-IS-10-10-20.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For service-rendering businesses (including EOR and staffing payroll services), the registration threshold is the 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption: the general limit of EUR 36,800 of annual taxable turnover (2024/2025 reference; increased to EUR 40,000 as of 2025 for certain qualifying SMEs per art. 293 B CGI) for providers of services; however, once the turnover exceeds this threshold, VAT registration is compulsory on the first euro of income with no further exemption; for non-resident supply of B2B services, the reverse-charge mechanism (Article 283-2 CGI) deems the French recipient liable and no voluntary registration threshold applies to non-established suppliers except under specific simplified regimes, so full French VAT registration is required at inception where the supplier has a French establishment or where the place of supply is France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the 'Réforme de la facturation électronique' (Law 2023-1322 and DGFiP specifications), as of 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered entities established in France must receive electronic invoices and must issue e-invoices in a structured XML format (Factur-X / UBL / CII) transmitted via the Portail Public de Facturation (Chorus Pro) or through an accredited Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP), with mandatory e-invoicing for large and mid-size enterprises by that date and for SMEs by 1 September 2027; real-time fiscal 'clearance' is achieved through the transmission of transaction-level data to DGFiP for VAT reporting (e-reporting) not through real-time per-transaction tax stamping, as in Italy or Latin America; API-only clearance applies to PDP and to selected large taxpayers and requires the OpenAPI v2 specification, SAML2/OpenID Connect authentication, and cryptographic signature per the Chorus Pro security model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT is available for exports of goods definitively leaving the EU, and for certain services directly linked to exported goods or to intangible supplies made to non-French taxable persons (Article 262-I CGI, Article 262-II CGI); an EOR or staffing agency may zero-rate only those services where the recipient is a business established outside the EU and the service is effectively consumed outside France per the general place-of-supply rule in Article 259-1 CGI, or where the services are directly related to the sale and transport of exported goods (freight inspection, customs brokerage) — payroll facilitation and workforce management services are generally not export-zero-rated unless the place of supply is the recipient's country under the B2B 'place of supply' rule, in which case the invoice must carry the French intra-community VAT number and a valid reverse-charge reference; strict documentary proof under Article 275 CGI and BOI-TVA-CHA-40 requires the exporter to hold evidence that goods left the EU within 90 days of despatch, including the export declaration ('l'exportation') dated by customs, the proof of physical removal from the EU, and any commercial contract identifying the French supplier.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — the 'Déclaration d'Exportation' (DAE, IE-507 XML format) lodged electronically via the DELTA-X system or a customs broker, containing the 8-digit export code 18101000 for temporary staffing services or the appropriate EC code, and validated with an MRN (Movement Reference Number)

Bill of Lading — the air waybill (AWB / LTA), ocean bill of lading, CMR or international transport document issued by the carrier, stating the shipper, consignee, nature of goods and the definitive destination outside the EU, compatible with the attached export declaration

Inward Remittance Certificate — a bank attestation of the foreign buyer's SWIFT MT103 payment or equivalent proof of provenance of funds evidencing a non-French counterparty and matching in amount and descriptive reference the export invoice and customs record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are scrutinized by the DGFiP's national audit directorate (DVNI) via documentary reconstruction tests; where the 0% rate is applied without the mandatory proof of exportation or where fraud is detected (faux export, fictitious freight, or chain circular invoices), the French tax administration imposes a 40% deliberate-understatement penalty (une majoration de 40% pour manquement délibéré) or an 80% penalty for organized fraud ('manœuvres frauduleuses', Article 1729 CGI, para. c), plus late-payment interest at the monthly rate of EURIBOR+5% (Articles 1727 and 1731 CGI), and a criminal fine of up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment of five years under Articles 1741 CGI (fraude fiscale), and the notified assessment may be escalated to the French courts; the DGFiP may refuse the VAT credit on such exports and retrospectively claw back all zero-rated output VAT as if it were payable at 20%, with no mitigation for good faith absent compliance with the documented export file under Article 275 CGI.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Euro operates under full capital and current account convertibility per EU single market rules. No prior approval required for profit remittances to non-resident shareholders. Hurdles limited to post-transaction beneficial ownership verification, economic substance attestation, and AMF reporting thresholds (€10,000 cash transactions).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Receipts credited directly to corporate bank accounts. FX conversion permitted only for commercial purposes; any transaction exceeding €10,000 must be reported to AMF with supporting documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for EUR-settlement platforms (Wise, Revolut Business). Legal constraints require French EMI authorization under PSD2 for payment initiation services; offshore digital EMIs must avoid unauthorized banking activities and comply with AMF licensing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital KYC and video verification permitted for corporate clients. Physical presence required only for high-value accounts, complex ownership structures, or elevated AML risk flags.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS extract, ownership chart, control agreements, and PEP screening
Bank statements, tax returns, capital contribution agreements, and third-party confirmations
Full sanctions screening report and adverse media clearance

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SEPA credit transfers (EUR) with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQU'. Verification via KYC, beneficial ownership, and economic purpose attestation. Wires must reference capital contribution agreement or invoice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for international disbursements; Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. EOR payroll settlements via local direct debit integration with licensed payroll providers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after fiscal year end (typically 30 June for calendar fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 10,000 EUR per month of delay; potential administrative dissolution if not filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owners Declaration Update (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or annually if no changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 10,000 EUR; possible strike-off for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Annual turnover > 50 million EUR, balance sheet total > 43 million EUR, or > 500 employees

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual filing or update of beneficial owners information to RCS; maintain current UBO register
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registre des mandataires sociaux)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% corporate income tax rate with 3.3% social contribution; R&D tax credit up to 5% of qualifying R&D expenses; innovation and competitiveness tax credit

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A / Déclaration de résultat - Impôt sur les sociétés; electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g. 30 April for calendar year-end 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss before adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, only French-source profits are taxable; adjust for permanent establishment attribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for depreciation, provisions, and other expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents limited to expenses related to French operations
Apply any applicable exemptions or incentives

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax computation including social contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may face additional withholding on certain payments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay, minimum 40 EUR per month, maximum 10% of tax; criminal penalties for evasion up to 5 years imprisonment and fines

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from French tax authorities; submit application form and supporting documents to claim reduced treaty rate; process through impots.gouv.fr portal or bilateral treaty procedures
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs; Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs; subject to arm's length conditions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 EUR (group turnover threshold triggering Local File and Master File requirements)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has implemented Economic Substance Regulations aligned with OECD standards; entities must maintain adequate economic substance in France for their core activities to avoid penalties, loss of treaty benefits, and potential recharacterization of transactions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions including fines up to 500,000 EUR or imprisonment up to 5 years, plus payment of evaded taxes with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, disqualification from corporate offices, and potential travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a company with no real economic activity or substance in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 10% of annual turnover, potential dissolution of the entity, and back taxation with penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal liability for debts and taxes; possible imprisonment for fraudulent management

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform due diligence, report suspicious transactions, or maintain proper beneficial ownership records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to 1 million EUR or 5% of annual turnover (whichever higher), plus criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment for willful non-compliance, and disqualification from management positions
